description: Research references for Myanmar keyboard layouts and legacy font profiles. This is an evidence index, not a keyboard, conversion table, or production parser configuration.

policy.pending_layouts: Keep all pending layouts, including Unicode-output and partial layouts. No layouts are excluded by this reference research.
policy.third_party_material: References and aggregate observations only. No third-party keyboard or converter tables are integrated.
policy.inspection: The supplied Windows installer and its components were inspected statically; they were not executed.
policy.distinctions: A physical keyboard, a font, text encoding, and embedded PDF subset bytes are different evidence. Similar names or direct slots do not establish complete equivalence.

text_tools.label_scope: These are converter selections, not verified names of separate physical keyboards. PDF1 is a special converter case, not a general PDF font profile.

ms_heavy.historical_observation: The changelog describes MS-HEAVY and MS-MOOM as font types added on 2 December 2006. It does not identify Microsoft as their maker or identify an associated keyboard.

static_profile_comparison.method: Compare entries in the converter's apparent parallel profile arrays corresponding to Unicode consonants U+1000 through U+1021. Exclude missing direct entries. No converter code was executed.
static_profile_comparison.limitation: These aggregate internal slot similarities do not establish keyboard equivalence, full encoding compatibility, contextual conversion behavior, or Microsoft provenance.

font_archive.note: Only the four named PostScript Type 1 font and metrics files were extracted into a temporary research cache; none were added to this repository. The archive's provenance and whether these are the exact versions targeted by the converter are not independently verified.
font_archive.encoding_array_observation: The font programs' own 256-position Encoding arrays define 127 positions for MS-HEAVY and 118 for MS-MOOM: 93 are defined in both, 34 only in MS-HEAVY, and 25 only in MS-MOOM. Both have nonempty glyphs at the converter's 33 comparable direct consonant slots.
font_archive.encoding_array_limit: Presence or absence of an internal font slot does not establish its Unicode meaning, the host application's font reencoding, or a physical keyboard. Do not assume that the two font programs have identical coverage or conversion rules.

ms_heavy.status: Found font programs matching both names. Their internal notices credit SUNNY and Hintha(r) Press, not Microsoft; this does not establish what MS stands for or rule out their use in Microsoft Office. An original document or associated keyboard has not been identified.

microsoft_windows.documentation_observation: The pinned layout HTMLs have identical illustrated key-state content apart from their titles and descriptions. This is not a runtime test of the two input methods or their composition and ordering behavior.
microsoft_windows.office_interpretation: Windows can supply a Myanmar font and input method without the user separately installing a font. Office can also use other fonts and keyboards; the application name alone does not determine the text encoding or keyboard.

microsoft_windows.word_example_limit: PDF creator fields and embedded font names are evidence of those files, not proof of original keystrokes or the keyboard that produced them.

wininnwa_book1_witness.outline_observation: The PDF subset glyph at raw byte 0x25 has matching contour topology and close shape to the reference WinInnwa font's U+00FA glyph (distance 0.00802 using the project's contour comparison). This adds an outline witness to the previously user-confirmed subset reading.
wininnwa_book1_witness.production_status: The current WININNWA_LEGACY_CODE_PAGE has no U+00FA entry. No mapping or runtime behavior was changed.
wininnwa_book1_witness.limitation: The PDF byte is subset-specific and is not the same as the font's character code. The ToUnicode bridge, font version, and context are evidence for this sample, not a universal byte map.

current_legacy_name_probe.method: Read the actual reference fonts' internal names and pass them to the existing isLegacyFontName function. Also probe detectLegacyLayoutFonts with synthetic no-ToUnicode PDF font dictionaries using WinAnsiEncoding. No scoring or production configuration was changed.
current_legacy_name_probe.synthetic_font_object_result: The simple Wwin and WinInnwa dictionaries were recognized as legacy; the simple MS-HEAVY and MS-MOOM dictionaries were not recognized by name.
current_legacy_name_probe.limitation: A positive name match is generic legacy-font recognition, not proof of a Wwin-specific decoder or correct output. Other existing PDF detection paths may flag a font based on its structure or ToUnicode map without identifying it as MS. The probes did not run the production Manager on a genuine MS or Wwin document.

win_and_wwin.naming_caution: WinMyanmar Systems is associated with WinInnwa, while an NFLCIME converter named winmyanmar has been identified by other researchers as Wwin-like. The name WinMyanmar alone does not identify a unique keyboard or font encoding.

reference_font_witnesses.attribution_in_font: Zaw Htut / SMMS Inc. with MCC

win_and_wwin.font_observation: The two font files have different names, attributions, and selected glyph outlines. Selected outlines from the WinInnwa PDF subset resemble the WinInnwa reference face more closely than the Wwin reference face; this supports separate profiles, not a universal font-version identification.

keyboard_references.name: myWin KeyMagic source
keyboard_references.observation: The source describes a Unicode layout designed to resemble WinMyanmar Systems' non-Unicode layouts, with changes, and declares Myanmar3 as its font family.

keyboard_references.name: ZawCode KeyMagic source
keyboard_references.observation: The source describes Zawgyi-style input with Unicode output.

keyboard_references.name: Keyman Burmese keyboards
keyboard_references.observation: Keyman describes myWin Extended as a simplified WinMyanmar-style Unicode layout and Myanmar3 SIL as a modified layout originating with Myanmar NLP using MSKLC.

keyboard_references.name: ThanLwinSoft Myanmar Unicode input guide
keyboard_references.observation: The guide describes myWin as loosely based on traditional WinMyanmar fonts and notes that Unicode input does not exactly match the older layouts and their modifier combinations.

direct_key_comparisons.scope: Normal and Shift printable keys in an empty context, compared against the already-generated KeyMagic draft outputs. Invisible spacing characters count as different. These counts do not test composition, other modifiers, or keyboard equivalence.

project_legacy_table_review_lead.scope: Static comparison of shared single-codepoint literal rules only; not the NFLCIME converter's full ordered execution and not a production Manager test.
project_legacy_table_review_lead.interpretation: The existing table labeled WinInnwa more closely resembles the referenced WinMyanmar literals in this limited comparison. This is a review lead, not proof of origin, complete profile identity, or a confirmed production bug. No parser or heuristics were changed.

wininnwa_base_bridge_witness.user_confirmed_reading: 0x17 = က in the context 17 25 = က္က
wininnwa_base_bridge_witness.outline_comparison: The subset 0x17 glyph and the reference WinInnwa U+0075 glyph had matching contour topology and normalized contour distance 0.00603. The Wwin_Burmese U+0075 comparison gave 0.07303; a single glyph does not identify a full font or encoding.
wininnwa_base_bridge_witness.unicode_keyboard_crosscheck: The retained ZawCode source's u key emits U+1000, mapped by the examined TharLon font to ka. This is a separate Unicode keyboard observation, not proof of the PDF's physical key or a conversion rule.
wininnwa_base_bridge_witness.limitation: The user-confirmed reading, subset-specific byte, PDF ToUnicode bridge, legacy font cmap entry and physical key position are distinct evidence layers. The ToUnicode bridge is not an independent keystroke record.

keyboard_font_crosscheck.scope: All 54 retained draft artifacts, declared-family metadata, local candidate font cmaps, selected regional key positions, and bounded KeyMagic/HarfBuzz context witnesses. Layouts and their original gaps are preserved.
highlights: The same U+1095 maps to a Shan digit glyph in TharLon and a dot-below glyph in the examined Zawgyi-One face; ZawCode and Zawgyi L also emit different raw code points for the same input sequence.

Two PaOh source layouts declare Myanmar3 and emit U+108F and U+AA7B, which are absent from the examined Myanmar3 family faces but present in separately named Myanmar3 PaOh, Padauk, and Pyidaungsu candidates. That does not prove a historical font assignment.

Two local Myanmar3 files have the same family/version metadata but different hashes and produce different HarfBuzz glyph sequences for a selected kinzi context. The cause and other rendering environments are unverified.

The separately supplied ZawCode binary and compiled source differed on 96 of 9,025 two-key outputs in this engine; the binary also produced an unknown-op warning, so other engine behavior remains unverified.
keyboard_font_crosscheck.boundary: Raw keyboard outputs, font cmap/glyphs, shaped glyphs, legacy Type 1 encoding slots and PDF subset bytes are distinct domains. No production heuristic or converter was changed.

next_evidence: A dated original MS-HEAVY or MS-MOOM DOCX/XLSX, PDF, or recorded keyboard sample with known font and source application. Type 1 font witnesses are available, but no original keyboard or document has been confirmed.
An original WWIN keyboard or document showing the keyboard name, font family, and known typed text.
The Ours-Unicode font file or a known document using it, and regional PaOh rendering examples for the declared versus candidate fonts.
Contextual keyboard probes and real word-level evidence before treating any source or font profile as equivalent.
